name: dsr_hunt_advisory_pack
description: Advisory vuln-hunting ideas for the DSR live hunt (NOT a sealed/source-backed pack). Priority-ordered. Only leading methods surface to the agent as OPTIONAL ideas; methodology is not restricted.

starter.applicability: Any firmware binary that may pass externally-influenced strings to a shell or command executor: web/CGI handlers, service daemons, update/diagnostic/management utilities.
evidence_requirements: Decompiled or disassembled call site of a command-executing function (system, popen, execl/execle/execlp, execv/execve/execvp, do_system, twsystem, ___system, or a vendor wrapper).
A concrete data path (xrefs / call path) from an untrusted input source to the command-string argument.
Pseudocode showing that sanitization/escaping between source and sink is absent, insufficient, or bypassable.
starter.label: Trace externally-influenced input into command-execution sinks (priority tier 1: remote command/code execution)
starter.limitations: Static reachability does not prove runtime exploitability; a path may be gated by callers, authentication, or input constraints not visible in one procedure. Treat as a hypothesis until a deterministic tool corroborates the path.
ordered_steps: Enumerate command-execution sinks: search_strings and list_procedures for system, popen, execve, execl, execlp, execvp, do_system, twsystem, ___system, '/bin/sh', 'sh -c'; record each call site with find_xrefs_to_name.
For each sink, read procedure_pseudo_code and identify the exact argument that becomes the command string.
Walk backwards with build_call_path and xrefs from that argument toward its origins (function parameters, globals, NVRAM/config getters, recv/read buffers, CGI getenv of QUERY_STRING/HTTP_* ).
Decide whether any reachable origin is externally influenced (network request field, uploaded/parsed file content, environment set by a request handler, UART/console).
Inspect intervening code for sanitization (whitelist, metacharacter rejection, fixed-format snprintf); note any that is missing or bypassable.

If an untrusted source reaches the command string without adequate sanitization, record the source, the sink call-site address, the call-path edges, and the unsanitized shell-metacharacter opportunity.
starter.reproduction_gate: Requires the sink call-site address, the source->sink call path, and the surrounding pseudocode; promotion requires independent host-side corroboration of the path (re-derived xrefs / call-path / bytes), not model assertion.
starter.source_summary: Standard command-injection source-to-sink methodology (CWE-78) applied to embedded/firmware binaries; synthesized from common practitioner practice, not executed from a single source.

starter.applicability: Any firmware component that reads data from outside the device or across a trust boundary (network, uploaded/received files, remotely-settable configuration, IPC).
evidence_requirements: Identified input-reading call sites (network, file/ingest, environment, NVRAM, IPC) with xrefs.
For each, the destination buffer/variable that holds attacker-influenced data, tagged as a taint origin.
starter.label: Enumerate untrusted input sources and tag taint origins
starter.limitations: A source being present does not mean it is attacker-reachable; confirm the interface is exposed and the path is not auth-gated before relying on it downstream.
ordered_steps: Network sources: find_xrefs_to_name for recv, recvfrom, read-on-socket, accept, and CGI/FastCGI getenv (QUERY_STRING, CONTENT_LENGTH, HTTP_*), plus web-server request structures.
File/ingest sources: fopen/open/fread/mmap of uploaded, received, or imported files, and archive/extraction/decompression routines.
Remotely-settable config sources: nvram_get/getenv/cfg_get whose values can be written through an exposed interface.
For each source, note the destination buffer and tag it as a taint origin for the sink-tracing and parser methods.
Prioritize sources reachable without authentication or before an auth check.
starter.reproduction_gate: Requires the source call-site addresses and the tainted destination buffers; this method feeds the sink-tracing and parser methods rather than producing a standalone finding.
starter.source_summary: Generic taint-source enumeration for firmware across network/file/config/IPC boundaries; synthesized practitioner methodology.

starter.applicability: Code that parses data received, uploaded, imported, or extracted from an external source: protocol parsers, file/image/config parsers, decompressors, firmware-update handlers (priority tier 2: remote ingested input).
evidence_requirements: The parser entry point and the untrusted buffer it consumes.
A length/count field from the input that drives a copy or index without validation against the destination size.
The specific copy or size-arithmetic operation that can overflow or under-validate.
starter.label: Review parsers of ingested/received data for memory-safety violations (priority tier 2)
starter.limitations: Bounds that appear absent in one procedure may be enforced by a caller; confirm the full path. Exploitability depends on memory layout not fully recoverable statically.
ordered_steps: Identify parser entry points from the input-source enumeration and from strings naming formats/protocols; read their procedure_pseudo_code.
Find unbounded or length-driven copies: strcpy, strcat, sprintf, memcpy/memmove with attacker-influenced length, stack buffers sized from input.
Check whether a length or count field read from the input controls a copy or index without validation against the destination size.
Look for integer overflow/sign-conversion issues in size computations feeding an allocation or copy.
Record the exact input offset/field, the vulnerable operation's address, and why validation is absent or insufficient.
starter.reproduction_gate: Requires the parser address, the unsafe operation's address, and the input field controlling it; promotion requires host-side corroboration of the bytes/call path.
starter.source_summary: Memory-safety review of untrusted parsers (CWE-120/CWE-787/CWE-190) in firmware; synthesized practitioner methodology.

starter.applicability: Whole-firmware or service-binary review to determine what listens on the network or LAN and which handlers process untrusted input (priority tier 3: exposed services).
evidence_requirements: Enumerated listeners/handlers: bind/listen ports, CGI/web routes, inetd/xinetd/init service registrations.
A mapping from each exposed entry to the binary/procedure that handles it, and whether it runs before authentication.
starter.label: Map exposed network/LAN service surface and route untrusted input to handlers (priority tier 3)
starter.limitations: Presence of a listener does not confirm external reachability in deployment; record the assumption about network exposure (internet / LAN / auth-gated).
ordered_steps: From the unpacked filesystem, read inittab, rcS/init scripts, inetd.conf/xinetd.d, service-manager units, and web-server configs (lighttpd/boa/mini_httpd/uhttpd) to list started services and listening ports.
In service binaries, find bind/listen/accept and CGI dispatch tables; map URL routes or command opcodes to handler procedures.
Mark which handlers run before authentication and which accept the largest or most-structured input.
Feed the highest-priority handlers into the command-injection and parser methods as starting points.
Record the exposed entry, its reachability (internet/LAN/auth-gated), and the handler address.
starter.reproduction_gate: Requires the service/handler addresses and the config evidence establishing exposure.
starter.source_summary: Attack-surface mapping for networked firmware services (OWASP FSTM surface mapping); synthesized practitioner methodology.

starter.applicability: Exposed services and login/auth routines that may contain hardcoded credentials, backdoor accounts, or bypassable authentication.
evidence_requirements: The auth/credential comparison site and the constant or logic involved.
The exposed entry that reaches it.
starter.label: Find hardcoded credentials, backdoors, and authentication bypasses in exposed services
starter.limitations: A constant string resembling a credential may be a provisioning default meant to be changed; distinguish a true backdoor from an initial default and state which.
ordered_steps: search_strings for credential-like constants, backdoor markers, and tokens; find format strings for password/login/admin handling.
Locate password/token comparison routines (strcmp/memcmp against constants, custom hash checks) and read their pseudocode.
Identify logic that lets authentication be skipped: default-true flags, magic parameters, debug/engineering modes, off-by-one in length checks.
Confirm the routine is reachable from an exposed service entry.
Record the constant/logic, its address, and the reaching entry.
starter.reproduction_gate: Requires the comparison-site address, the constant bytes, and the exposed reaching path.
starter.source_summary: Hardcoded-credential and auth-bypass review for firmware (CWE-798/CWE-288/CWE-489); synthesized practitioner methodology.

starter.applicability: Every confirmed hypothesis that will be submitted as a finding, to make it mechanically verifiable and promotable rather than a narrative claim.
evidence_requirements: A structured claim carrying concrete, tool-re-derivable anchors: byte offsets, call-path edges, and xref lists.
starter.label: Package a finding so an independent tool can re-derive it (how to write it up)
starter.limitations: A finding without re-derivable anchors stays a model hypothesis and cannot be promoted; narrative alone is not evidence.
ordered_steps: State the vulnerability class, the affected binary/member, and a one-line impact tied to a priority tier (remote command/code execution first).

Populate a structured claim object the host can re-derive mechanically: for each assertion include at least one of - read_bytes anchors as {offset, length, expected-hex}; build_call_path edges as [from_addr, to_addr]; xrefs as {from, target} lists.
Give the source->sink path explicitly: the untrusted source, the sink call-site address, and every intermediate edge.
State the exact reproduction gate: what a verifier must independently confirm (bytes at offsets, path edges) to raise the finding above a model hypothesis.
Submit via refall-submit with the claim object and evidence refs; do not assert verification yourself - leave promotion to an independent tool/human check.
starter.reproduction_gate: The claim must contain at least one non-empty, tool-re-derivable anchor (bytes, call-path edges, or xrefs); otherwise the finding is held.
starter.source_summary: DSR finding-packaging convention aligned to the independent-check promotion gate; synthesized for this harness.
